{{Quote|Confer on you the level of Jedi Knight, the Council does. But agree with your taking this boy as your Padawan learner, I do not.|Yoda speaks with Obi-Wan Kenobi in the Turret Room|audio=Yoda-Confer.flac|<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
The '''Turret Room''' was a serene chamber within the [[Theed Royal Palace]], in the [[capital]] [[city]] of [[Theed]] on the [[planet]] [[Naboo]]. It was attached to a small temple used to revere ancient [[Monarch of Naboo|rulers of Naboo]] and was originally constructed by [[King]] [[Jafan]]. In [[32 BBY]], members of the [[Jedi High Council]] were granted use of the Turret Room to privately mourn the loss of their comrade [[Qui-Gon Jinn]] while visiting Naboo for his [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn|funeral]]. [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] then met with [[Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in the Turret Room to announce his promotion to the rank of [[Jedi Knight]].

==Description==
[[File:Turret_Room_tower.png|thumb|right|180px|The Turret Room resided in a tower of the Theed Royal Palace.]]
The Turret Room was a serene chamber attached to a small temple within the [[Theed Royal Palace|Royal Palace]] in the [[city]] of [[Theed]], [[capital]] of the [[planet]] [[Naboo]].<ref name="SWCL2016" /> The square room was built within a tower on the edge of the palace. Three of the room's four walls held large [[Viewport|windows]] with [[Color|white]] paneling that looked out over a cliff edge, with four brown columns raised on plinths in each corner of the chamber between the different sets of windows. The room's floor was made up of gray stone tiles, with a square pattern in the center of the floor made up of alternating lines of dark-gray and white tiles.<ref name="TPM" />

In [[32 BBY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY]].</ref> the chamber was furnished with a pair of low, backless chairs in front of one window and four high-backed chairs set before the opposite window. The final window had a table below it, complemented by four chairs, and set with a white cloth and small [[plant]] pot.<ref name="TPM" />

==History==
[[File:Kenobi_and_Yoda_Turret_Room.png|thumb|left|250px|Yoda meets with Obi-Wan Kenobi in the Turret Room.]]
The Turret Room and attached temple were built by [[King]] [[Jafan]], the first ruler of Naboo's [[Great Time of Peace]]. The temple came to be used by the [[Monarch of Naboo|monarchs]] of the [[Royal House of Naboo]] to honor the great rulers of the past.<ref name="SWCL2016" /> In 32 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> the [[Jedi High Council]] was granted use of the Turret Room to privately mourn and celebrate the life of their fallen colleague, the [[Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn]], when they traveled to Naboo to attend his [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn|funeral]].<ref name="SWCL2016" />

Shortly before the [[Jedi funeral|funeral]] took place, [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]] met with Jinn's [[Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], in the Turret Room and informed him that the Council had granted him the rank of [[Jedi Knight]]. Yoda then told the newly knighted Jedi that he personally disagreed with Kenobi honoring Jinn's last wish to take on the young [[Anakin Skywalker]] as a Padawan but that the Council did not, and so Kenobi would be allowed to [[Jedi training|train]] the boy.<ref name="TPM" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Yoda paces back and forth during this sequence, and I was amused to see that Frank wrote his dialogue along the inside of the hole in the floor, each line written where Yoda stops to speak them.|Visual effects supervisor [[John Knoll]]|<ref name="365 Days">''[[Creating the Worlds of Star Wars: 365 Days]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Yoda_Puppet_Turret_Room.png|thumb|right|250px|The Turret Room set was raised to allow Frank Oz to control Yoda from beneath.]]
The Turret Room first appeared in the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="TPM" /> After principal photography for the film had already been completed and editing begun, director [[George Lucas]] felt that an additional scene was needed, and so the scene set in the Turret Room was added to the film in [[March]] [[1998]] as part of pickup shots being filmed at [[Leavesden Studios]].<ref name="365 Days" />

The small set was built in its entirety at the studio and was raised five feet off the ground so that [[Frank Oz]], the puppeteer voicing and controlling Yoda, could fit beneath the floor. A section in the middle of the room's floor was removable to allow Oz to work, and the puppeteer wrote his lines along the inside of the hole at the points corresponding to where Yoda stopped pacing and spoke.<ref name="365 Days" />

In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the Turret Room was first identified by name in the [[2016]] reference book [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']].<ref name="SWCL2016" /> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the [[2000]] reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', written by [[Kristin Lund]].<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref>
